newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Comalco sees signs of improved result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Comalco sees signs of improved result.

text.p: Aluminium producer Comalco Ltd said on Wednesday it had seen signs of an improved result for calendar 1997 and that its result in the first three months of the year had been much improved.
It said it was experiencing stronger demand for aluminium.

"I am pleased to report that the financial performance of the company for the first three months of 1997 has been much improved," said chairman Leigh Clifford told the annual meeting. "We have made a reasonable profit in the first quarter and the early signs indicate an improved result for the full year in 1997," Clifford said
"The market for alumina continues to be firm and we are experiencing stronger demand for aluminium," Clifford said.
He said London Metal Exchange stocks at the end of March had fallen to 855,000 tonnes, down from December's level of 951,000 tonnes.
The LME price for march was 75 U.S. cents and the average for the year had been 74 U.S. cents, already an improvement on last year's average of 70 U.S. cents, Clifford said.
"Aluminium demand is strong in Asia and North America and the outlook for the industry is robust," he said.
"We are cautiously optimistic of maintaining our current level of performance throughout 1997," he said.
Comalco, 67 percent owned by RTZ-CRA, reported a loss of A$17.4 million for calendar 1996.
Comalco shares were eight cents firmer at A$6.50 at 10.40 a.m. (0040 GMT).
